page: Amazon Web Services m8id.8xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud server powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. The platform couples this compute tier with 128 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core.

Integrated directly into the host hardware, the instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 15 Gbps baseline network allocation. It does not contain discrete GPU hardware, relying entirely on the Intel Xeon CPU for processing and matrix acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show strong performance in Geekbench single-core (2,208.0) and multi-core (18,435.0) metrics, high throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (34.28 GB/sec), and top-tier execution in text processing benchmarks.

Data throughput testing demonstrates balanced system resource utilization. Memory subsystem benchmarks show 2558.45 GB/sec cached read throughput and 179.94 GB/sec large-block uncached read speeds. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 225.5 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures 59.28 GB/sec. Micro-model LLM text generation shows strong efficiency at 374.61 tokens per second on small 135M parameter models, though performance levels normalize to median tiers on larger models like the 70B parameter architecture.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the m8id.8xlarge is characterized by dense local NVMe storage combined with high memory frequencies and dedicated CPU resources without hypervisor overhead. Because local NVMe storage is bundled directly on the instance, it provides low-latency disk access compared to network-only attached storage. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include static web serving, high-performance caching tiers, data compression pipelines, staging environments, and database workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance driven by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring 16 physical cores with two threads per core and 480 MB of L3 cache, the system is backed by 128 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory and 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a baseline network throughput of 15 Gbps and omits dedicated GPUs. Performance testing shows strong results across Geekbench single-core, multi-core, and PassMark CPU metrics, paired with high-throughput compression and static web serving speeds of 59.28 GB/sec. Small-model inference and text processing perform in the upper tiers, while uncached memory bandwidth and multi-core stress-ng tests achieve standard baseline levels. The instance is suited for relational databases needing direct NVMe scratch space, enterprise application servers, and high-concurrency web serving.
